title: Spread a prescribed generic normalization and completion diagram
statement:
Let $f:X	o S$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation and $\eta$ a generic point of an irreducible component of $S$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $K$ be a field equipped with an embedding of $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $U_0$ is an affine open neighbourhood of $\eta$, and $g_0:V_0	o U_0$ is finite, surjective and universally injective, with $V_0$ reduced affine. Suppose $\eta_0$ is a generic point of an irreducible component of $V_0$ over $\eta$, and $e:\kappa(\eta_0)\simeq K$ is compatible with the specified embedding of $\kappa(\eta)$ under the residue-field map of $g_0\circ(U_0\hookrightarrow S)$. Write $X_K=X_\eta	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume the following explicit generic diagram is supplied. A finite family of integral closed subschemes $C_i$ of $X_K$ has pairwise distinct underlying irreducible components and exhausts all components. There are isomorphisms from $Y_i$ to the normalizations of $C_i$, dense open immersions $j_i:Y_i	o B_i$, finite separable extensions $L_i/K$, morphisms $q_i:B_i	o\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, and structure maps $p_i:Y_i	o\operatorname{Spec}K$. Each $Y_i$ is nonempty; $q_i$ is smooth, projective and geometrically irreducible; and $\dim B_i\leq1$. The normalization morphisms $Y_i	o C_i	o X_K$ have composite structure map $p_i$, and $j_i$ followed by $q_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L_i	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ is $p_i$. The given map $
u_\eta:\coprod_iY_i	o X_K$ is exactly the coproduct of these normalization morphisms. The maps $p_i$, $B_i	o\operatorname{Spec}K$, $\operatorname{Spec}L_i	o\operatorname{Spec}K$, $\coprod_iY_i	o\operatorname{Spec}K$, and $X_K	o\operatorname{Spec}K$ are all locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The indexing family is empty exactly when $X_\eta$ is empty [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-sc-normalization] [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] [def-pc-projective-morphism]. There exist an open neighbourhood $U\subset S$ of $\eta$, a finite surjective universally injective morphism $V	o U$, a finite family of finite etale morphisms $T_i	o V$, and commutative diagrams over $V$ $$\coprod_iY_i\xrightarrow{
u}X_V:=X	imes_SV,\qquad Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i	o T_i	o V$$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], with the following properties. The map $
u$ is finite and surjective; each $j_i$ is an open immersion; $Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and surjective; $\overline Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres of dimension at most one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There is an open $W\subset X_V$ such that $W_i:=
u^{-1}(W)\cap Y_i$ meets every fibre of $Y_i	o T_i$, and $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is a thickening, meaning a closed immersion surjective on underlying points [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. No density assertion is part of this statement. The finite family may be empty.

proof.text: Use the supplied compatible residue-field isomorphism to identify the generic fibre over the cover with the given K-base change of X_eta. The prescribed generic diagram supplies the normalization components and completions; no generic completion existence theorem is needed in this statement.

The reduced affine model has field stalk at eta_0. Apply the proved generic-residue-field affine-limit theorem to obtain a cofiltered affine-neighbourhood system with this generic residue-field spectrum as its limit. Identify that field with K using the supplied compatible isomorphism. Apply object descent to the finitely presented generic schemes while keeping X as its prescribed model, morphism descent to all arrows, and eventual equality to the commuting triangles. A common smaller affine neighbourhood works for the finite diagram. All objects are qcqs, and all arrows are locally finitely presented by finite presentation over a finite-type intermediate algebra.

Over the generic field $\nu$ is finite and surjective: it is the normalization of the reduction followed by the surjective closed immersion of the reduction. Use the existing normalization theorem and finite composition for this assertion. Descend finiteness and surjectivity of $\nu$, openness of each $j_i$, finite etaleness of $T_i\to V$, smoothness and surjectivity of $Y_i\to T_i$, and smoothness and properness of $\overline Y_i\to T_i$, using the respective cited descent statements. Their qcqs and local finite-presentation hypotheses were established in the preceding step; the weaker local finite-type hypotheses also hold. There are only finitely many maps, so take common refinements successively. Finiteness and surjectivity persist by their base-change lemmas, smoothness and open immersion by the eventual conclusions of the two new descent statements; etaleness is smooth relative dimension zero and is unchanged under restriction of base. Properness, defined using the diagonal and universal closedness, is likewise unchanged under base restriction. The given projective completion morphisms are proper before this descent, by projective implies proper.

For each $i$, $T_i$ has precisely one point $\eta_i$ above $\eta$, with residue field $k_i$. Apply local constancy of geometric component count to the proper smooth finite-presentation morphism $\overline Y_i\to T_i$. The count at $\eta_i$ is one, so there is an open neighbourhood on which all fibres are geometrically connected. Apply upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension to obtain an open neighbourhood on which the fibres have dimension at most one. Remove from $V$ the images under the finite maps $T_i\to V$ of the closed complements of these neighbourhoods. Those images are closed and avoid $\eta$, so this is an allowed shrinking. Thus all fibres now have both required properties. Properness plus smoothness gives finite presentation here: the objects are qcqs and smooth implies locally of finite presentation.

Apply the reduced algebraic normalization theorem to $(X_\eta)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its dense normal open has normalization an isomorphism. View this open on $X_\eta$, whose reduction has the same underlying space. The normalization map above this open is then the inclusion of its reduction, a closed immersion surjective on points. Choose a quasi-compact dense subopen $W_\eta$ there: take finitely many affine neighbourhoods, inside that normal open, of the generic points of the finitely many components indexed by the normalization. Its inverse image meets every $Y_{i,\eta}$. By the scheme-over-limit lemma $X_\eta$ is the inverse limit of the qcqs $X_{A_a}$. Descend $W_\eta$ to a quasi-compact open $W$ at a stage using quasi-compact-open descent. The inverse image of $W$ under the finite $
u$ is also qcqs, and its map to $W$ is locally of finite type. Closed-immersion descent therefore makes $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ a closed immersion after a further localization. It is surjective by base change of the surjective $
u$, so is a thickening, with no square-zero assertion.

Put $W_i=\nu^{-1}(W)\cap Y_i$. The map $W_i\to T_i$ is open: it is the restriction of a smooth morphism, smooth implies flat and locally of finite presentation, and such maps are open. Its image contains $\eta_i$ by construction of $W_\eta$. Since $T_i\to V$ is finite, remove from $V$ the closed images of the complements of these open images. After this shrinking every $W_i\to T_i$ is surjective.

Make every cover shrinking downstairs by removing the finite image of its closed complement, and choose a principal affine refinement. The restriction remains finite, surjective and radicial. If the generic family is empty, eventual surjectivity of its empty coproduct forces X to be empty at a stage, so the empty open gives the claimed thickening.

theorem exists_good_curves_spread_generic_completion
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (η : S) (hη : ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents S, IsGenericPoint η Z)
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (S.residueField η) K]
    (U₀ : S.Opens) (hηU₀ : η ∈ U₀) (V₀ : Scheme.{u}) (g₀ : V₀ ⟶ U₀.toScheme)
    [IsAffine U₀.toScheme] [IsAffine V₀] [IsReduced V₀]
    [IsFinite g₀] [Surjective g₀] [UniversallyInjective g₀]
    (η₀ : V₀) (hq : (g₀ ≫ U₀.ι) η₀ = η)
    (hη₀ : ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents V₀, IsGenericPoint η₀ Z)
    (e : V₀.residueField η₀ ≃+* K)
    (he : e.toRingHom.comp
      (((S.residueFieldCongr hq).inv ≫ (g₀ ≫ U₀.ι).residueFieldMap η₀).hom) =
        algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)
    (hcurves :
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (hC : ∀ i, IsIntegral (C i))
        (c : ∀ i, C i ⟶ pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K))))
        (Y B : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
        (e : ∀ i, Y i ≅ @Scheme.normalization (C i) (hC i))
        (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ B i)
        (L : Fin n → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (L i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra K (L i))
        (q : ∀ i, B i ⟶ Spec (.of (L i)))
        (p : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Spec (.of K))
        (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)))),
        (∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (c i) ∧
          Set.range (c i) ∈ irreducibleComponents
            (pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K))) : Scheme.{u})) ∧
        Function.Injective (fun i ↦ Set.range (c i)) ∧
        (∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents
          (pullback (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K))) : Scheme.{u}),
          ∃ i, Set.range (c i) = Z) ∧
        ν = Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ (e i).hom ≫ @Scheme.fromNormalization (C i) (hC i) ≫ c i) ∧
        (∀ i, Module.Finite K (L i) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable K (L i) ∧
          IsOpenImmersion (j i) ∧ DenseRange (j i) ∧ Nonempty (Y i) ∧
          Smooth (q i) ∧ IsHProjective (q i) ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible (q i) ∧
          topologicalKrullDim (B i) ≤ 1 ∧
          (e i).hom ≫ @Scheme.fromNormalization (C i) (hC i) ≫ c i ≫
            pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K))) = p i ∧
          j i ≫ q i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i))) = p i ∧
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation (p i) ∧ QuasiCompact (p i) ∧ QuasiSeparated (p i) ∧
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation
            (q i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) ∧
          QuasiCompact (q i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) ∧
          QuasiSeparated (q i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) ∧
          LocallyOfFinitePresentation (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) ∧
          QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i)))) ∧
          QuasiSeparated (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (L i))))) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation (Sigma.desc p) ∧
        QuasiCompact (Sigma.desc p) ∧ QuasiSeparated (Sigma.desc p) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)))) ∧
        QuasiCompact (pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)))) ∧
        QuasiSeparated (pullback.snd (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.residueField η) K)))) ∧
        (n = 0 ↔ IsEmpty (f.fiber η))) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U) (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ U.toScheme),
      IsFinite g ∧ Surjective g ∧ UniversallyInjective g ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (T Y Ybar : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
        (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Ybar i)
        (p : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ T i)
        (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)),
        IsFinite ν ∧ Surjective ν ∧
        (∀ i, Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ pullback.snd f (g ≫ U.ι) = j i ≫ p i ≫ t i) ∧
        (∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ Etale (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (j i ≫ p i) ∧ Surjective (j i ≫ p i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Smooth (p i) ∧ IsProper (p i) ∧
          ∀ s : T i, GeometricallyConnected ((p i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
            topologicalKrullDim ((p i).fiber s) ≤ 1) ∧
        ∃ W : (pullback f (g ≫ U.ι)).Opens,
          (∀ (i : Fin n) (s : T i),
            ∃ y : (j i ≫ p i).fiber s,
              ((j i ≫ p i).fiberι s ≫ Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) y ∈ W) ∧
          IsThickening (pullback.snd ν W.ι)
